Subject: Dune Capital SecQ - clarifications on retention and erasure for Hosted API

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the RFP response. A few follow-ups from our security questionnaire around your Hosted API: we need concise, definitive answers we can include in our compliance package. The three areas we care most about are:

1) Where does customer data live by default (region/replica topology)?
2) How long do you retain request/response payloads, logs, and audit trails?
3) What is the deletion/erasure lifecycle (including backups) and what evidence do you provide after an erasure request?

I attached the SecQ PDF with the specific line items. Could you also confirm whether any user input is used for model training by default?

Appreciate a short, actionable reply so we can close the loop for our InfoSec review.

Best,
Samir
Security Lead | Dune Capital

Subject: Re: Dune Capital SecQ - clarifications on retention and erasure for Hosted API

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask; see answers below. I kept each point short and included a single-line evidence link or next step. Monica (product infra) is cc'd on the technical bits. If you want an official attestation doc we can generate one after the PoC.

1) Data residency / topology:
- Default: customer data for new Hosted API tenants is stored in the account’s selected cloud region (we currently offer US-West, US-East, EU-West). Primary storage is in-region; we maintain an asynchronously replicated read-only replica in a separate availability zone within the same region for durability.
- Cross-region replication is not enabled by default; it requires an explicit contract-level option.
- Evidence/next step: we can provide a region map + bucket locations for the PoC.

2) Retention windows (hosted API):
- Request/response payloads (prompt + model output): retained for 14 days by default for debugging and short-term analytics.
- Audit logs & operational traces (route-level metadata, timestamps, error codes): retained 90 days by default.
- Tokenized billing counters and aggregate usage metrics: retained 2 years for billing and quota reconciliation.
- Ephemeral mode: customers can opt into Ephemeral Mode at account level; in this mode, prompts/responses are not written to persistent stores (kept in memory only for the lifetime of the request) and no request payloads are retained. Audit logs remain (minimal) to satisfy SLO & billing but contain no full-text payloads.
- Evidence/next step: attached retention matrix (redwood_retention_matrix.xlsx) shows exact TTLs and the fields we redact from audit logs.

3) Deletion / erasure lifecycle & backups:
- Live deletion: upon a customer erasure request (API or support ticket), data scoped to the request (customer prompts and stored outputs) is removed from live stores within 24 hours and a deletion job is created.
- Backups & snapshots: encrypted snapshots are rotated and retained for up to 30 days as part of our disaster recovery policy; data will be removed from subsequent backups during regular snapshot rotation. For customers requiring shorter backup windows we offer a managed backup-shortening option in enterprise contracts.
- Cache & KV: ephemeral KV caches used for prefix caching are in-memory by default and are drained within seconds after eviction policies; we do not persist those caches to long-term object storage unless a customer opts into persistent caching.
- Evidence: after completion we can provide a deletion receipt with a deletion job ID + timestamp and a short attestation (signed PDF) for compliance.

4) Training usage:
- By default, customer-provided prompts and outputs are NOT used to improve public models or our internal training datasets. If a customer opts into a feedback program for model improvement, that is explicit and contractually scoped.

If you want, Monica can provide the exact S3/GCS key naming conventions and the internal playbook we follow when a deletion job is run. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you prefer to run through the items live.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Samir — quick technical clarifications to Rafael's answers below; forwarding the exact runbook excerpts so your security team can see the operational steps.

Quoted for context:
> - Live deletion: upon a customer erasure request (API or support ticket), data scoped to the request (customer prompts and stored outputs) is removed from live stores within 24 hours and a deletion job is created.
> - Backups & snapshots: encrypted snapshots are rotated and retained for up to 30 days as part of our disaster recovery policy; data will be removed from subsequent backups during regular snapshot rotation.

Concrete runbook summary (excerpt):
- Step 1: Validate scope (account ID + object keys). Operator creates Deletion Job ID and enqueues to the deletion service.
- Step 2: Deletion service atomically tombstones object metadata and issues background erasure across primary blob stores (in-region) — estimated completion for live objects: <24 hours.
- Step 3: Workflow marks all associated ephemeral caches and worker shards for immediate eviction.
- Step 4: Snapshot/s3 lifecycle: snapshots older than 30 days are deleted by lifecycle policy; any retained snapshot that contains the subject data will be overwritten on the next snapshot rotation. Snapshot pruning is automated but the window is up to 30 days.
- Step 5: Post-erase validation: integrity check of object index + optional log-scan to confirm absence of full-text prompt in audit indices (we keep hashed references).

Additional notes:
- For high-assurance erasure we offer a certificate workflow: we run the job, run a secondary index scan, and produce a signed PDF attesting to removal. That runs within 48 hours of job completion and includes the Deletion Job ID and hashes of affected object keys.
- If Dune Capital requires shorter backup retention or immediate snapshot scrub, we can include that in a contract addendum.

Let me know if you want the full runbook exported (we'll remove internal-only operational flags).

—Monica
Senior Product Manager, Infra
Redwood Inference
